newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SHORT AUSTRALIAN DEBT FINDS LONG END A DRAG.
newsitem.headline: SHORT AUSTRALIAN DEBT FINDS LONG END A DRAG.

text.p: *Short Australian debt futures held modest gains at midday, but were unable to progress an early advance with the long-end remaining twitchy ahead of U.S. retail sales data for July.
*Westpac consumer confidence survey at 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT)

Short Australian debt futures held modest gains at midday, but were unable to progress an early advance with the long-end remaining twitchy ahead of U.S. retail sales data for July later on Wednesday.

Comments by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane on Tuesday were seen not ruling out the possibility of a further easing in monetary policy and at worst official rates were likely to be on hold at 5.0 percent for a considerable time, analysts said.
"Macfarlane's comments certainly gave the market a lift and were a lot less negative that we expected him to be," said one trader at the short-end of the curve.

Macfarlane said the RBA did not have a growth ceiling and that the economy could grow 4.5 percent or more over the next few years without sparking inflation. He also did not see monetary policy placing any contraint on growth.
The September bill futures contract pared back an early an early mark-up, but at 95.06 was still trading at a discount to official 5.0 percent cash rate.

Meanwhile, longer dated stock remained hampered by the persistent heavy tone of U.S. Treasuries, which has soured the local tecnhical outlook and saw 10-year bond futures edge through at 4-1/2 month rising trendline.

The yield curve steepened sharply as the short-end outperformed against longer maturities, and also outpaced the rest of the dollar bloc. The long-end also reversed an initial margin widening against as the U.S. weakened further in Tokyo trading.
